prompt_transform.guidance: Choose shot scale based on what must be understood first: place, relationship, action, or face.
prompt_transform.template: Camera/Framing: define shot scale for {subject} in {scene}, making the first visual priority explicit.

negative_constraints: Do not mix wide, close-up, and macro instructions in one single-frame node unless sequencing is required.
Do not omit shot scale when the prompt asks for cinematic output.
quality_checks: Shot scale is named or clearly implied.
The shot scale supports the visual priority.

source_refs.label: StudioBinder shot size guide
source_refs.note: Shot size is a foundation of visual grammar.

prompt_transform.guidance: Name one primary camera move and connect it to the subject action or emotional reveal.
prompt_transform.template: Camera/Framing: camera movement {camera}; it follows or reveals {action} with {motion} pacing.

negative_constraints: Do not stack unrelated moves such as whip pan, dolly, drone, and macro in one shot.
Do not use aggressive camera movement for a restrained emotional beat unless contrast is intentional.
quality_checks: Exactly one primary camera move is dominant.
Movement direction and speed are clear.

source_refs.label: StudioBinder camera movement guide
source_refs.note: Camera movement changes perspective, space, and time.

source_refs.label: Runway Gen-3 prompting guide
source_refs.note: Camera movement can be explicitly described in video prompts.

prompt_transform.guidance: Use camera angle to clarify vulnerability, neutrality, dominance, disorientation, or observation.
prompt_transform.template: Camera/Framing: choose angle for {subject} that expresses the relationship or power dynamic in the beat.

negative_constraints: Do not use Dutch tilt as generic cinematic decoration.
Do not use low angle unless power, scale, or threat is intended.
quality_checks: Angle has a stated narrative reason.
Angle does not conflict with subject emotion.

source_refs.label: Adobe camera angles guide
source_refs.note: Different angles alter interpretation and emotional impact.

prompt_transform.guidance: Use lens and depth cues only when they support scale, intimacy, compression, or environment readability.
prompt_transform.template: Camera/Framing: lens/depth cues keep {subject} readable while preserving {scene} context.

negative_constraints: Do not add lens jargon if it conflicts with the described frame.
Do not force shallow depth when environment detail is essential.
quality_checks: Lens/depth cue has a visual purpose.
Subject and environment hierarchy is clear.

source_refs.label: Adobe wide shot guidance
source_refs.note: Focal length and depth support scale and setting.

prompt_transform.guidance: Turn every node into a shot with subject priority, frame intent, shot scale, and camera purpose.
prompt_transform.template: Camera/Framing: shot intent makes {subject} readable in {scene} with a clear camera purpose.

negative_constraints: Do not call a prompt cinematic without specifying frame intent.
Do not choose camera language that distracts from the node goal.
quality_checks: Camera purpose supports the node target.

source_refs.label: StudioBinder camera shots guide
source_refs.note: Shot size, framing, movement, and angle shape audience perception.
